target_customer: Mom-and-pop neighborhood stores (kirana) in Pakistan that buy inventory, and the brands and distributors that sell to them
problem: Small Pakistani stores waste hours dealing with dozens of suppliers, wait for salesmen to visit, get late or wrong deliveries and learn prices only at delivery.
business_model: B2B marketplace and distribution: Tajir buys from brands, sells to stores on margin and delivers next day; later adds software for brands and financial services
product_category: B2B retail inventory marketplace and distribution app

founders.name: Babar Khan
founders.background_notes: Brother of Ismail Khan. Their father ran an FMCG retail distribution business for three decades (TechCrunch, June 2020). Education and prior employers not found in an opened source. Later press describes him as CEO.

founders.name: Ismail Khan
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. Education and prior employers not found in an opened source.

competitors.name: Udaan (India)
competitors.what: B2B marketplace for small retailers in India, cited by TechCrunch as the comparable model

competitors.name: Bazaar (Karachi)
competitors.what: B2B ordering marketplace for grocery stores, closed pilot in Karachi during the 2020 lockdown

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app plus pricing catalog, but real difficulty was operations: sourcing, warehousing and last mile delivery across Lahore for thousands of small stores.

defensibility.rationale: Software was copyable; advantage came from supplier relationships, delivery network and store base (15,000 stores by June 2020 per TechCrunch), which a funded rival could rebuild.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge in the period covered; funded startups Bazaar and Retailo (founded 2020) entered the same segment in 2020 and 2021.

market_need_then: About 2 million neighborhood stores in Pakistan buying through fragmented, undigitized distribution; TechCrunch (June 2020) reported most sales are offline and no major e-commerce player existed.

branding.name_origin: Tajir is the Urdu and Arabic word for merchant (Rekhta dictionary); no founder statement about choosing it was found.
branding.domain_note: Company site is tajir.app, not tajir.com.

identity.logo: Green wordmark with square icon variants per the media kit file names
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical, focused on next day delivery and price transparency

brand_strength.rationale: A fitting local word, but no sources show brand driven growth; traction came from price and delivery.

outcome_analysis: Tajir was a Lahore B2B inventory marketplace for neighborhood stores, founded by two brothers whose father ran FMCG distribution. It raised a $1.8M seed in June 2020 after YC and a $17M Series A led by Kleiner Perkins in June 2021, among the largest Pakistani rounds that year. It remains listed as active with about 50 staff, but a Profit report grouped it with startups that quietly cut staff as capital tightened, and no later round was found.
notes: Founding year: YC page says 2019, some press says 2018. One aggregator (TrySignalbase) says $19M Series A; $17M is backed by many outlets. CB Insights lists about $18.95M across six rounds, so other small rounds may exist. A Profit snippet mentions discreet layoffs, undated. TechCrunch 2020 said Tajir had no major competitor. Education reported by one profile site (Tufts, Berkeley MBA, Brown) was not verified in an opened source so it is left null. Persana pages naming a different CEO are treated as unreliable.
